senses.gloss: (I)--a sage who knew the power of विष्णु's yoga. भा. II. 7. ४४.
(II)--a son of Ulmuka and पुष्करिणी. भा. IV. १३. १७.

(IV)--a son of Nakta and Druti: A राजऋषि and an अम्श of Hari; a महापुरुष who ruled his kingdom righteously and with devotion to Hari. His name is sung in an ancient गाथा, as the upholder of धर्म, Vedas, ब्रह्मणस् and यज्ञस्. His queen was गायन्ती who was mother of three sons Citraratha and others. At the end of [page१-515+ २७] his rule, he renounced the throne and sought refuge with Hari. भा. V. १५. 6-१४: X. ६०. ४१: Br. II. १४. ६८: वा. ३३. ५७. Vi. II. 1. ३८.
(V)--though lord of seven द्वीपस्, he was not content. He wanted more territory. भा. VIII. १९. २३; XII. 3. १०.

(VI)--a son of (इला) Sudyumna and Lord of Dak- षिणापथ;
1: भा. IX. 1. ४१. M. १२. १७.
king of the eastern kingdom with its capital Gaya;
2: Br. III. ६०. १८.
a राजऋषि.
3: वा. ८५. १९.
Performed a big sacrifice and gave lavish gifts to all ब्रह्मणस्; even gods were pleased and granted a boon perpetuating his name by a city गयापुरि; attained विष्णुलोक.
4: वा. ११२. 1-6.
(VII)--a son of Angirasa and ऊरु. M. 4. ४३.
(VIII)--a son of बलकाश्व. वा. ९१. ६१.
(I)--a R. visited by बलराम. भा. X. ७९. ११. [page१-516+ ३५]

(II)--(च्) the kingdom of; sacred for श्राद्ध offering. धर्मपृष्ट, Brahmasaras, and गृध्रवट are chief places here; capital of Gaya; परशुरान performed श्राद्ध here.
1: M. १२. १७. Br. III. १३. १०४: १९-11: ४७. १७: ६०. १९: वा. ८५. १९.
A पितृतीर्थम् being the residence of पितामह; a गाथा says that any one son may visit गया and satisfy all पितृस्.
2: M. २२. 4-6 and २६: ११०. 2; १९२. ११: २०४. 8: २०७. ४०.
Fit for श्राद्ध; a man devoted to गयाश्राद्ध must dress himself in beggar's garments, circumambulate the ग्राम, and the next one with shaving and begging money; श्राद्ध in ब्रह्मकुण्ड and other places; going to Dhar- maranya after worshipping गदाधर; feed the Brahmans there without enquiring into their family, conduct or learn- ing; offer पिण्डस् in गयारूप, even for unknown cognates and names; पिण्ड for one's own self with तिल; by this even heinous crimes are mitigated; a superior तीर्थ; best in Makara, eclipses of the sun and moon, and Caitra and Preta- पक्ष (महालय); others are अधीमास, birthday, the even- ing of Guru and शुक्र, the stay of बृहस्पति in Simha which is once in twelve years.
3: वा. ७७. ९७: ८०. ४५: ८३. १२-44.
The face of the Veda;
4: Ib. १०४. ७७.
शम्भु, विष्णु and Ravi; sacred to Gaya.
5: Ib. ११२. २०.
(III)--six in number, गायागय, गयादित्य, गायत्री, गदाधर, गया, गयासुर, all tending to salva- tion. वा. ११२. ६०.
--(गायन्ती-ब्र्। प्।), wife of Gaya (s.v.) and mother of three sons. भा. V. १५. १४.
--sacred to Hari. भा. VII. १४. ३०.
--the legend about गया. वा. ११२. ६२, ६७. [page१-517+ ३५]

--origin of; the austerities of गयासूर here bearing a stone on his head. Here गदाधर stood steadfast lest he should move; on this ब्रह्मा performed a sacrifice; shaving and fasting are prescribed in तीर्थस् but not for this place; measurement 2(1/2) क्रोश; गयाक्षेत्रम् 5 क्रोशस् and गयाशिर 1 क्रोश, the best of all तीर्थस्. वा. १०५. 4-४६.
--the north sun. वा. १०९. २१.
--after the name of king Gaya. वा. ११२. 5.

--pilgrimage to गया; preliminaries; per- formance of श्राद्ध, going round the village, travel to another village and so on, every day without begging food, etc.: purity and selflessness to be maintained; reaching गया, bathing and performance of श्राद्ध according to his Veda शाख; the next day visit to Pretaparvata, bath in ब्रह्मकुण्ड and the offer of पिण्डस् in other places. See गय। वा. ११०. 1-9.

--one क्रोश in extent;
1: वा. १०५. २९.
श्राद्ध there lifts १०० generations.
2: Ib. १०५. ३१.

--a सूक्तम् of the साम Veda to be recited in tank ritual;
1: M. ५८. ३६; वा. 9. ४८.
from the first face of ब्रह्मा.
2: Vi. I. 5. ५३.

(IV)--रौद्री, contemplated by ब्रह्मा in the २१स्त् kalpa; गौः in Lohita kalpa.
2: Ib. २३. ६९.
(II)--one of the seven horses yoked to sun's chariot; expiation for sin; in Sandhya worship. Br. II. २१. ११३; २२. ७२; २६. ४४; IV. 7. ६९. Vi. II. 8. 5; IV. 6. ८९.

(III)--a शक्ति;
1: Br. IV. ४४. ८६.
mind-born daughter of ब्रह्मा, inseparable from him; a goddess enshrined in the Vedas; as the basis of dharma in the भागवत P.
2: M. 3. ३२; 4. 7, 9 and २४; ५३. २०; १७१. २३.
--in गया; bathing at and offering of प्रातस्सन्ध्या or morning prayers. वा. ११२. २१.
--a भार्गव gotrakara. M. १९५. २३; वा. ८३. ६१.
--Unfit for श्राद्ध. वा. ७९. ६९.
